item.title: Spain to hold three days of mourning for victims of high-speed train crash
item.description: MADRID, Jn 20 (NNN-AGENCIES) — Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has announced three days of national mourning for victims of a high-speed train crash that killed at least 40 people. Sanchez also promised to get to the bottom of why the two high-speed trains collided in southern Spain, as rescuers continue to search the wreckage. item.title: Czech gun violence: Gunman kills one, wounds six others including town mayor in town hall before killing self
item.description: PRAGUE, Jan 20 (NNN-AGENCIES) — A shooting at a Czech town hall left one person dead and at least six others, including three police officers, wounded on Monday, authorities said, adding that the gunman had also killed himself. Police said they had secured the building in Chribska, 110 km north of Prague. “Currently, nothing suggests any terrorist or extremist motive. item.title: Japan’s Remaining Twin Pandas To Depart For China On Jan 27
item.description: TOKYO, Jan 20 (NNN-NHK) – Giant pandas Xiao Xiao and Lei Lei, currently residing at a zoo in Tokyo, will depart for China on Jan 27, marking the first time in about half a century that Japan will be without any pandas, local media reported. The twin pandas will be transported from the Ueno Zoological Gardens to Narita airport, near Tokyo, to fly to China and are scheduled to arrive on Jan 28, Kyodo News reported. item.title: Gold prices hit new record high
item.description: MOSCOW: Gold prices jumped more than two percent on Tuesday, surpassing the US$4,700 mark per troy ounce for the first time in history, according to trading data, Sputnik/RIA Novosti reported. As of 5:10 GMT, the price of gold futures for February on the New York Comex exchange increased by US$108.71, or 2.37 percent, from the previous close to US$4,704.11 per troy ounce, thus setting a new all-time high. item.description: PAPEETE (French Polynesia), Jan 20 (NNN-AGENCIES) — France’s navy has seized 4.87 tonnes of cocaine, believed to be bound for Australia, from a fishing vessel in the South Pacific, French officials said. item.title: Bursa Malaysia closes lower, composite index drops below 1,700 level
item.description: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia’s main index closed lower today, falling below the 1,700 level due to continued profit-taking activities and weak performance in regional markets amid rising geopolitical tensions that affected investors’ risk appetite. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 13.27 points, or 0.77 per cent, to 1,699.06 from Monday’s closing level of 1,712.33. The market indicator opened lower, down 1.31 points to 1,711.02, its highest level today, and hit a low of 1,695.
